title: What 3 minutes near Chernobyl's Elephant's Foot does ☢️
subject: radiation
description:
How long would you dare to stand there? 👇

The Elephant's Foot is a mass of melted nuclear fuel, sand and concrete under Chernobyl's Reactor 4. In 1986 it could give you a lethal dose of radiation in about 3 minutes. Here is what it does to the human body, and how strong it is today.

Sources: Wikipedia, "Elephant's Foot (Chernobyl)" (radiation measurements 1986–2016, AK-47 samples); Nautilus, Kyle Hill, "Chernobyl's Hot Mess, 'the Elephant's Foot,' Is Still Lethal" (2013).
tags: what radiation does to your body

scenes.text: You'd absorb a lethal dose here in about 3 minutes.
This is the Elephant's Foot: melted fuel and concrete under Chernobyl's Reactor 4.
In 1986 it flowed like lava. Workers found it that December.
It gave off up to 10,000 roentgens an hour. After 30 seconds, dizziness hits a week later. After 2 minutes, your cells start breaking down.
It was so hard that scientists shot off samples with an AK-47.
By 2016, readings were down to about 1 percent of that. Still dangerous.
